samples.xml_description:
<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel-to-Serial Converter</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel input data.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="CNT_WIDTH">Width of the counter register.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[CNT_WIDTH-1:0]">Counter register for tracking the current bit position.</reg>
        <reg id="valid">Valid signal to indicate the availability of serial output.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width_description="[3:0]">Register to store the parallel input data.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Assigning the most significant bit of the parallel input to the serial output
        assign dout = data[3];
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or active low reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // If reset is active, initialize the counter register to 0
                cnt <= {CNT_WIDTH{1'b0}};
            end else begin
                // If the counter register is equal to 3, update the data register with the parallel input,
                // reset the counter register to 0, and set the valid signal to 1
                if (cnt == 3) begin
                    data <= d;
                    cnt <= {CNT_WIDTH{1'b0}};
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    // Otherwise, increment the counter register by 1, set the valid signal to 0,
                    // and shift the data register to the left by 1 bit
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    data <= {data[2:0], 1'b0};
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Assigning the valid signal to the valid_out port
        assign valid_out = valid;
    </implementation>
</module>
